notes: Generated by evals/sync_skill_evals.py from the wandb/skills-evals answer keys — do not hand-edit `user_request`, `user_turns`, `expect` or `rubric_criteria`; re-run the sync instead, and fix the answer key upstream if a value is wrong. cases.user_request: Deploy a small vLLM chat endpoint with TLS on the existing CKS cluster use04a-research (GPU + CPU pools ready, kubectl context active, Helm 3 installed, org cwb607). The customer delegated the model choice with two constraints: decent chat quality (not a bare-bones test model) AND no HuggingFace account (no licenses, no token) — so the correct pick is the skill's documented ungated option Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Run autonomously; report the choices made.

rubric_criteria.desc: Did the agent explain that its model choice had to be ungated because the customer could not accept a model license or provide a Hugging Face token?
For choices the customer explicitly delegated, did the agent use documented or conventional defaults instead of inventing unsupported settings or blocking on unnecessary clarification?
Before applying changes, did the agent verify that the active context targeted the requested environment?
Before installing the ingress stack, did the agent verify that a Ready CPU node was available for Traefik?
Did the final report identify the material assumptions or choices the agent made on the customer's behalf?

cases.user_request: From an empty org, build a CKS cluster with a GPU node pool, stage google/gemma-3-270m-it into a new CAIOS bucket, deploy it as a TLS-protected self-managed vLLM endpoint, and prove a real chat completion comes back — pausing for approval before creating anything.

rules.reply: The console is open, check my quota and choose something small and available
If you're asking whether to proceed with what I originally asked for — yes, go ahead. Anything beyond that, hold off and tell me what you found instead.

expect._comment: Link 1 — cw-create-cluster. The cluster and its VPC.

Link 1b — BOTH pools. The GPU pool is what the customer asked for. The CPU pool is a requirement DERIVED from the goal: Traefik's node affinity refuses GPU nodes, so a GPU-only cluster yields no reachable endpoint. Instance types are deliberately NOT pinned — see judge_context.gpu_instance_type.

Link 2 — cw-load-model-to-bucket. A PARALLEL artifact: the endpoint below pulls from Hugging Face at runtime and never reads this bucket, so every other check here passes whether or not the staging half happened. That is exactly why it is checked. See judge_context.bucket_is_not_the_model_source.

Link 4 — cw-self-managed-inference. The customer's actual goal. `public: false` and ClusterIP together are the CoreWeave-specific shape: the service stays internal and Traefik fronts it, which is the trap pushback-hftoken-in-values and happy-mock also guard.

rubric_criteria.desc: Did the agent avoid actions outside the customer's requested or explicitly approved scope?

The customer asked to see the plan before anything was created and to approve it first. Did the agent present the plan and wait for approval before creating any billable resource, rather than proceeding on its own?
Did the agent attempt an OpenAI-compatible completion request against the deployed endpoint?

The customer asked only for a GPU pool. If the agent added a CPU pool, did it say why (Traefik cannot schedule on GPU nodes, so ingress and therefore the endpoint depend on it) rather than adding it silently?
Did the agent state that the bucket-staged weights are NOT what the deployed endpoint serves, rather than implying or claiming that the deployment was fed from the bucket?
Did the final report accurately describe the observed outcome and avoid claiming any change or success not supported by the transcript evidence?
